title: Wilson Junior College symphony band and boyhood friend Joe Williams
summary: Playing bass in the junior college band while gigging on piano, and his long friendship with Joe Williams from high school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So when you were playing bass, were you playing both piano and bass, or did you just concentrate on the bass?
No, the bass belonged to the Chicago school system, and when I went to junior college in Chicago, Wilson Junior College, they had a little symphony band there, you know?
Uh-huh.
And I would play bass in the symphony band. We'd do, "The Bohemian Girl," and, "La Boheme," and a
lot of things, you know? And then playing piano, you know, gigging at the same time. And just try -- well, we were all trying to make ends meet. See, Marty Young, Joe Williams.
He wasn't Joe Williams yet, was he? Didn't he have -- wasn't his last name something else?
Yeah. It started with a G.
I can't remember what it is, but I think it's in the encyclopedia.
Yeah. It started with a G. Goreed (PHONETIC).
Yeah.
In fact he was the first one to sign my graduation annual, the year book, when you graduate from high school or something, you know?
You and Joe went to high school together?

Yeah, we went to high school together and we used to live next door to each other, when we were both about 15 years old, because I think -- Joe just had his birthday. We're the same age, only two weeks apart.
Yeah, and Joe's two weeks older than you, right?
Yeah.
That's right, Joe's birthday was last week.
Yeah, so -- and we just never knew that this thing -- as far as our partnership, musically, was going to develop this way.
It's a long association.
Yeah, we used to --
From 15 year olds to 'The Tonight Show' now.
Yeah. Now we're pushing 1980.
(Laughter)
